text:
maria: Heads-up — hit a sharp tail-latency spike in the EU-west dedicated slice around 18:03 UTC. 95th->99.9th jumped ~4x for short bursts, looks like a single node (az3b) NVLink/egress hotspot. Logs in thread.
raj: saw the alert, seconding node hotspot. Is this noisy GPU compute (batch job) or network egress coupling?
chris: quick probe shows NVLink retries + PCIe RT counters bumped on az3b. stack traces point to a single tenant doing heavy tensor-swap roughly at 18:02.
maria: devops-bot posted the original alerts:
devops-bot: ALERT: eu-west/az3b dedicated-slice latency_tail > 99.9pct for 5m. metrics: gpu_pcie_rt>300, nvlink_retries>120, tenant=alpha-corp
sophie: if it's one tenant, we should isolate at allocation-level then bail to fallback pool. Can we do a live carveout? Prefers soft-reserve rather than full preempt.
chris: we can toggle routing policy to steer new allocations away from az3b and mark the node for warm-drain. Example patch:
```yaml
routingPolicy:
  avoid_nodes: [az3b]
  fallback_pool: shared-gpu-eu
  preempt_mode: soft
  token_bucket_limit: 500
```
raj: token_bucket_limit tweak might limit bursty tenants quickly. We used 200 before and it caused too many fallbacks; 500 seems safer.
maria: timeline? We need to avoid cascading preemptions during peak. Also need a plan if fallback pool overheats.
leo: cost note — holding a 1-GPU warm reserve in eu-west is ~14% uplift on committed monthly spend. But it kills 2x outage risk if we avoid noisy spillback. Tradeoff: reserve vs >99.9 tail SLA hits.
sophie: propose short playbook:
1) mark az3b avoid_nodes for 30m
2) move alpha-corp allocs to soft-preempt and redirect new requests to shared-gpu-eu
3) run nvlink perf-capture on az3b for 10m
4) if repeats within 2h, quarantine az3b and create temporary dedicated carveout in eu-west-b
5) post-mortem and tenant throttle suggestion
chris: nvlink capture command (run on ops host):
```
ssh ops@az3b "sudo nvlink-stats --capture 60 --out /tmp/nvlink-18-03-utc.gz"
```
maria: done steps 1+2. Routing switch applied, new allocations avoid az3b. Shared pool spike up ~12% but holding for now.
devops-bot: ACTION: routingPolicy updated by maria (avoid az3b). Fallback pool: shared-gpu-eu. Watcher enabled.
raj: can someone run a quick tenant attribution check to see which job triggered it? I can correlate with scheduler logs.
chris: pulled scheduler logs: tenant alpha-corp job 8421 did large swap at 18:01:54, repeated 3x.
leo: flagged alpha-corp SE and account owner. Recommend temporary throttle (rate limit tokens) + suggestion to use KV-cache warmers.
sophie: add a short-term quota: `tenant_rate_limit: 0.7` for alpha-corp on shared pool, will soften after 1h if stable.
maria: I sent DM to account owner and infra-sre to schedule deeper probe tomorrow. For now metrics look back to normal after 25m.
raj: follow-up actions: (a) nvlink capture artifact in /tmp; (b) run perf counter aggregation across az3 cluster; (c) review token-bucket defaults for dedicated pools; (d) cost analysis for warm reserve variant.
chris: putting minimal perf artifact link here: s3://infra-artifacts/eu-west/az3b/nvlink-1768509999.gz
leo: I'll crunch cost uplift numbers for 1/3/5 GPU warm reserve models and share by EOD.
sophie: also propose we add an automated noisy-tenant detector: simple rule: if one tenant accounts for >60% of NVLink retries on a node for 1m => auto-soft-isolate and token-bucket clamp.
maria: agreed. Filed quick ticket: INFRA-4521 "auto-isolate noisy tenant via nvlink heuristics". Assigning to raj+chris.
raj: ack. will iterate on detection threshold and false-positive cases P0.
maria: thanks all. keeping this thread pinned until post-mortem. :thumbsup:
